## Fit linear regression model with `lm()`

You need to provide the function lm with two arguments. The first one should be a formula and the other the dataset. Formulas are written in the following form:

**`y-variable ~ x-variables`**. Between each x-variable there should be a `+`. For instance:

```{r}



```

If I want to add an interaction term between the variables area and cooling I separate them with a `*` instead of a `+`. Or alternatively add a third variable `area:cooling.`

```{r}



```


### Print summary measures of the fit of the model with `glance()`

I can also get some summary statistics about the model with the function `glance()`.

```{r}
glance(m1)




models <- list(m1, m2, m3, m4, m5,m6)
model_names <- paste0("Model_", 1:6)


summary_table <- purrr::map_df(models, ~glance(.x), .id = "model") %>%
  mutate(model = model_names,
         formula = map_chr(models, ~deparse(formula(.x))))


summary_table %>%
  select(formula,  r.squared, adj.r.squared)

```

### Residual analysis with `plot()`

Finally you can get residual analysis plots with the function plot().

```{r}
plot(m2)
```

If you only want one of the plots you can specify which with the argument `which.`

```{r}
plot(m2, which=1)

```

### Derive predictions from a model with `predict()`

In order to use you regression model for prediction you can use the function `predict().` You need two arguments the first is your regression `model`, the second is the `data` you want to make predictions for. More specifically the `data` need to be a data.frame or tibble and include the explanatory variables used in the regression model. This can be used for one observation or an entire dataset.

Let's say I want to use the regression model to predict the price of a house that has an area of 2500 square feet and central cooling, then I can use the following code:

```{r}
datanew<-tibble(area=2500,cooling="central")
predict(m2,datanew)
```
